newsitem.title: UK: Physical coffee trade dampened by futures rally.
newsitem.headline: Physical coffee trade dampened by futures rally.

text.p: A sharp rebound in futures to six-week highs this week dampened activity on the physical coffee markets, traders said on Friday.
The physical sector noted strong interest on outright and differential basis for the first few days after the New Year.
"But since the market rallied in London...the actual trading of physical coffee in Europe is somewhat quiet," said one.
Futures values were boosted on Wednesday by a burst of investment fund short-covering, triggered by a prospect of a lower-than-expected crop in top grower Brazil.
On Tuesday an official at Brazil's Industry and Commerce Industry said it was working with a preliminary range of just below 20 million 60-kg bags for 1997/98.
This compared with trade estimates of up to 30 million bags although local grower forecasts have been much lower.
The benchmark March contract in London reached a high of $1,335 a tonne on Thursday, a peak since November 29, from a life low of $1,203 on Tuesday.
While physical buyers and sellers retreated, traders said many roasters and shippers took advantage of the futures rally to fix their contracts.
"The focus of attention has been the hedging of coffee into the London market," an London trader said.

"In relative terms, robusta remains fairly cheap," he said. "I think the general opinion was that $1,200 robusta coffee has got very, very cheap and so I imagine roasters have taken advantage of that."
A Swiss-based trader said origin sellers had turned cautious and were awaiting much better levels.
"Also, roasters have not yet accepted the idea of having to pay higher prices," he said.
Looking ahead, traders said the London futures could consolidate their recent gains before testing higher ground.
"I think the market can consolidate around this level and then push a little higher," said one physical trader.
The recent market weakness widened robusta's discount to arabica to 62 cents a lb, basis March.
The differential has fallen back to 59 cents and traders now expect the level to narrow further to 50-55 cents.
European coffee demand is expected to remain strong with traders expecting a small growth this year. The current cold snap across Europe is seen helping coffee consumption.
"I think consumption figures are quite healthy throughout Europe including East Europe...There's small but positive growth and I think consumption is relatively good," said one.
Differentials for physical coffee were said to have remained largely steady to better this week.
Uganda robusta (screen 15) is about $40 under London on an FOB basis, against $60.
Colombian Excelso was quoted 8-10 cents over New York's March contract (FOB) while Costa Rican hard bean (new crop) was quoted 8-11 cents over New York.
Indonesian EK1 beans (new crop) were quoted at $160-$170 under London on an FOB basis and March delivery at $100 under.
The new crop is due for delivery from May onwards. The nearby January and February coffee are almost sold out.
Cameroon Grade One was quoted at $60 over London CIF Europe, down from $70 last month while Ivory Coast grade two was quoted at level CIF Europe. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
